notes: The connector runs only inside the dedicated server as a BepInEx plugin. Players use plain vanilla Valheim; nothing is installed on clients, and every Takaro token and cloud setting stays on the dedicated server.

Server chat works through one 'Takaro' entry the server adds to the player list it sends to clients (outgoing packet only; the server's own player list and history never contain it). Vanilla clients send each chat line once per player-list entry and only render chat from listed senders, so player chat reaches the server even when a player is alone and server messages render as normal chat with the sender name.

chat-message and player-death come from routed Say, ChatMessage, and OnDeath RPCs, accepted only when the packet's claimed sender equals the authenticated peer it arrived on and, for Say and OnDeath, the target is that peer's own character. Spoofed senders are rejected. Copies of one chat line are collapsed within 3 seconds.
Game events are queued until Takaro accepts identify and flushed afterwards, so events raised while identifying are not lost.
getPlayer is implemented by filtering the dedicated server player list, but its final Takaro response shape has not been independently live-proven, so it remains unsupported.

getPlayerLocation uses only a real ready-peer/public observation or a fresh 30-second player-keyed last-known observation. If neither exists, a required-coordinate payload with error is rejected by current Takaro Generic.requestFromServer rather than returned as a position.
getPlayerInventory is unsupported: Valheim keeps inventories in the client profile, and the dedicated server only sees equipped visuals. The connector refuses rather than fabricating an inventory.

giveItem drops the items at the player's server-known position; the vanilla client's auto-pickup puts them in the player's bag. Takaro returns the empty success payload, so the API alone cannot tell whether the player has picked them up yet.

sendMessage is server-owned: the server sends a normal chat line from the Takaro player-list entry, using opts.senderNameOverride when set and otherwise the configured chatSenderName (default Takaro). Global messages go to every peer; recipient messages go to that peer only.
teleportPlayer routes Valheim's built-in RPC_TeleportTo to the server-known character ZDO owner.

Item and entity names in listItems, listEntities, giveItem resolution, and events are the English display names from the game's own Localization (for example 'Crude Bow', 'Raspberries') rather than prefab tokens such as item_bow.

entity-killed coverage is partial. The event comes from the creature's network object when its owning game destroys it: the creature carries Attackers<playerName> marks and a kill-style modifier; the killer is the destroying player if it hit the creature, else the only player that hit it, and several hitters with none the destroyer are not guessed. A creature killed by a single blow carries no mark on the server, so that kill is credited only if its ragdoll appears from the same game within 8 seconds, that player started a weapon attack within 4 seconds before, and stood within 8 m (50 m with a bow, crossbow or staff). The weapon is the killer's equipped right or left item display name (the bow for ranged), or Unarmed.

Player lifecycle frames are derived from dedicated-server player snapshots. Turn-3 Takaro eventSearch persisted two player-connected and two player-disconnected events; transport logs still claim only that a frame was written, not persistence acknowledgement.

listLocations is schema-fallback: turn 4 live-proved the official raw Generic Connector action/schema with 11293 nested server-owned locations in a 1815046-byte response, but Takaro 0c63cf1c Generic.listLocations throws NotImplementedError, so the standard Takaro route is unavailable pending upstream support.

getMapInfo and getMapTile are part of the exhaustive Takaro 0c63cf1c action list but unsupported at the dedicated-server-only boundary because Valheim exposes neither client map metadata nor rendered map tiles there.

2026-09-02 acceptance run: banPlayer and unbanPlayer are live-supported. A live Takaro request wrote Steam_76561198000735875 into Valheim bannedlist.txt, disconnected the player without crashing the headless server, was read back by listBans with the accepted DTO shape, and was then removed so listBans returned an empty array.

2026-09-02 acceptance run: banPlayer discards the ban reason. A ban requested with reason 'acceptance test' was read back by Takaro listBans as reason ''. Valheim's native ban list stores only one player identifier per line, so the connector has nowhere to persist a reason.

2026-09-02 acceptance run: kickPlayer is live-supported. A live Takaro request logged 'kicked Hehe (Steam_76561198000735875). Reason: acceptance kick test.', getPlayers dropped to zero, and the headless dedicated server stayed alive because the built-in Kicked RPC is used instead of a direct ZNet.Disconnect(peer).

2026-09-02 acceptance run: listItems and listEntities are live-supported through the standard Takaro route. Takaro does not request either action until its sync job runs, so a newly registered game server shows an empty catalog until then; triggering syncItems/syncEntities returned 821 item prefabs and 101 character prefabs, which Takaro persisted.

2026-09-02 acceptance run: shutdown is live-supported. A live Takaro request wrote its success response frame first, then logged 'executing scheduled shutdown on the Unity main thread'; Valheim performed a clean ZNet shutdown and the dedicated server process exited.

2026-09-02 acceptance run: restart resilience verified. After a dedicated-server restart the connector re-identified without config changes and events resumed, with a fresh player-connected persisted by Takaro and module commands still executing.

2026-09-02 acceptance run: the full in-game shop purchase path is live-verified. With economyUtils installed, a player typing '@shop 1 1 buy' completed a Takaro shop order, had 100 currency deducted, and received the goods. Shop deliveries use giveItem, so purchased items land at the buyer's feet and auto-pickup collects them.
